1  HON'BLE AVNISH SAXENA, J. 
1.
Heard Sri Amit Srivastava, learned counsel for the applicants, Sri Puneet Srivastava, learned counsel for the opposite party no.3 and learned A.G.A. for State.

3. The instant application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been moved with a prayer to quash the proceedings of Case No.392/IX/06 (State Vs. Gajendra Singh Chauhan and others), arising out of Case Crime No.39 of 2005, under Sections 498A, 323 IPC and Section 3/4 of D.P. Act, Police Station Surir, District Mathura.

entities.text: Case No.392/IX/06 (State Vs. Gajendra Singh Chauhan and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel for the applicants submits that it is matrimonial case wherein parties have entered into compromise.
The FIR has been registered for the offence under Sections 498A, 323 IPC and Section 3/4 of D.P. Act by the father of the opposite party no.3.
Further contended that the applicant no.1 and opposite party no.3 are husband and wife and in compromise, they have buried their hatchet and residing together since 2006.
He further submits that the opposite party no.2 has passed away.

The compromise is at page no.35, which is in the shape of affidavit filed by the opposite party no.3 stating therein that due to some matrimonial dispute, she went to her parental home and her father in fit of anger, has lodged the FIR.
He further discloses that she does not want to proceed with the case.
Further submits that the matter is of the year 2005 and after moving application under Section 482 Cr.P.C., proceedings has been stayed since 2009.
Hence, seeks indulgence of this Court.
4. Learned counsel appears for the opposite party no.3 submits that her client being the wife does not want to proceed with the case.
The opposite party no.2 has expired.
He admits the factum of affidavit filed by the opposite party no.3 before the court, who herself was victim.
Further submits that in the counter affidavit, the death certificate of the opposite party no.2 is annexed at page no.12 disclosing that the opposite party no.2 passed away on 18.02.2021.
5. This Court has considered that the matrimonial case is ended in compromise as the parties have buried their hatchet long back.

6. In the case of Jasmair Singh and another Vs. State of Haryana and Another (2022) 9 SCC 73, the Supreme Court has observed that in matrimonial cases, if the parties have buried the hatchet and decided to give quietus to the proceedings, the exercise of section 482 Cr.P.C. (528 B.N.S.S.) for quashment of criminal proceedings, is eminent.

entities.text: Jasmair Singh and another Vs. State of Haryana and Another (2022) 9 SCC 73
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 7. Thus, the charge sheet and the proceeding arose out of case crime number mentioned above are hereby quashed.
Consequently, the proceedings of trial also quashed.
8. The application u/s 482 Cr.P.C. is allowed accordingly.

(Avnish Saxena,J.) September 8, 2025 Mini  Gajendra Singh Chauhan And Others vs State Of U.P.And Others on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163729672/
